sents.t: “Have you heard the news?” Mr. Brooks asked me on Monday.
“The city wants to build a parking lot in Maple Park.”
Maple Park is small, but it’s the heart of our neighborhood.
Rosa has walked Max there every day for ten years, and children have played under its old oak trees for generations.
On Thursday evening, about sixty neighbors came to a meeting at the community center.
A woman from the city council explained the plan.
“Downtown has become very busy,” she said.
“People can’t find parking.”
Then neighbors raised their hands one by one.
Rosa spoke about the trees.
A young father said his kids had nowhere else to play.
Even Lily, who rarely speaks in public, suggested a different location: the empty land behind the old train station.
Finally, Mr. Brooks stood up.
“I’ve lived on Maple Street for forty years,” he said.
“I’ve seen many changes, and most of them were good. But we can’t plant a hundred-year-old tree again.”
Everyone clapped.
The council member promised to study Lily’s idea.
A month later, we got a letter.
The city has accepted the plan: the parking lot will be built behind the train station.
Maple Park is safe.
